items.text: Understand what SSH is and why it is used for remote server access
Explain the difference between password-based and key-based SSH authentication
Describe the role of private key vs public key in SSH authentication
Understand the three Linux permission types: read, write, execute
Understand the three Linux permission categories: owner, group, others
Read and interpret a permission string like drwxr-xr-x
Understand what umask is and how it affects default permissions
Generate an SSH key pair using ssh-keygen with RSA 4096-bit encryption
Copy a public key to a remote server using ssh-copy-id
Connect to an EC2 user account using SSH with a private key
Enable password-based SSH authentication by editing sshd_config
View file permissions using ls -l and ls -ld
Change file permissions using chmod (both symbolic and numeric methods)
Change file ownership using chown and chgrp
Troubleshoot common SSH errors like Permission denied and duplicate key names
State the numeric values for read (4), write (2), and execute (1)
Calculate chmod octal values for common scenarios (755, 644, 600, 400)
Identify what SUID, SGID, and sticky bit do and when to use each
Explain the result of umask 022 on new files and directories
Describe why Amazon Linux disables password authentication by default
